subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode for HIPAA workload (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anna Bergstrom <anna.bergstrom@healthcareinc.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up + next steps from today's discovery call

Hi Anna — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and next steps from the call so we have alignment:

What we heard:
- Use case: patient triage and clinical summarization that will process ePHI (notes, lab results).
- Compliance drivers: HIPAA + need for a signed BAA, SOC 2 Type II evidence for our platform, audit logs accessible to Healthcare Inc security team.
- Deployment preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, but you mentioned Private VPC/on-prem is a hard requirement if customer systems store PHI at rest.
- Expected traffic: initial pilot ~5-10 reqs/sec with bursts to 40 reqs/sec; retention: 90 days of logs for audit.

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Can you confirm where PHI will be stored/staged? (client-side only, or will Redwood-hosted storage be used?)
2) Do you require inbound/outbound firewall restrictions (specific IP allowlists) for the inference endpoints?
3) Any specific audit/registry requirements beyond SOC2 (e.g., HITRUST, internal audit cadence)?
4) Procurement timeline and required paperwork for a BAA/POC.

Attachments: redwood-hipaa-overview.pdf (high-level controls + deployment options).

Proposed next steps:
- Anna to confirm PHI flow and list of infra/network constraints by EOD Thurs (2026-02-24).
- Internal: loop in Dev (cc) for architecture Qs and Rishi for pricing/SLA exceptions.
- If PHI will remain in your environment and only tokens sent to our Hosted API, we can proceed with Dedicated. If PHI will be persisted in Redwood-managed storage, Private VPC or on-prem will be required and we'll prep BAA + SOC2 evidence.

Happy to hop on a 30-min technical follow-up next week. What times work for you?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Anna Bergstrom <anna.bergstrom@healthcareinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Healthcare Inc Procurement <procurement@healthcareinc.com>
Date: 2026-02-24T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today's discovery call

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below:
- PHI flow: For the pilot, PHI will be de-identified prior to transmission in most cases, but we do have a small subset of workflows where ePHI will need to be processed (consented research cohort). For those, we cannot have PHI stored in any third-party managed persistent storage.
- Network: We require IP allowlisting and an SFTP endpoint for batch uploads.
- Audit: SOC 2 Type II attestation is required. HITRUST is not required today, but our internal audit team will want to review logs quarterly.
- Procurement: Procurement needs a draft BAA and initial pricing for Dedicated capacity and Private VPC options to present to their review board. Target decision: end of Q1 (by 2026-03-31).

Can you send SOC2 evidence and a draft BAA? Also schedule a technical call with Dev to walk through the PHI paths next week.

Anna
Anna Bergstrom
Head of Security & Privacy (Product) | Healthcare Inc
anna.bergstrom@healthcareinc.com

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Anna Bergstrom <anna.bergstrom@healthcareinc.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-27T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today's discovery call

Hi Anna — great to e-meet you. A few technical clarifications and proposals from our side:

1) Deployment options summary:
- Hosted API (standard): fastest to start, no persistent PHI storage by default; suitable if you can guarantee de-identification client-side.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): customer-dedicated runtime; can be configured to avoid persistent storage, with IP allowlisting and private peering options. Good middle-ground for predictable throughput.
- Private VPC / On-prem: full customer-managed networking; we can deploy a private control plane and/or on-prem inference nodes. Required if PHI must never leave customer-managed storage.

2) SOC2/BAA: We can provide SOC2 Type II attestation (link below) and a standard BAA draft. For BAA execution we typically use DocuSign — I can start that once we have contact from procurement.

3) Audit logs & retention: We support per-customer audit logs with configurable retention; 90 days is straightforward. Logs can be exported to your S3 or Syslog endpoint for quarterly audits.

4) Next steps:
- Please share a data flow diagram (redacted if needed) showing where ePHI originates and any intermediate storage.
- Procurement contact for DocuSign BAA: procurement@healthcareinc.com (cc'd by Anna).
- I'll attach a sample SOW/POC template for your legal team: dap-sow-template.docx

Happy to take 30 min next Tue (2026-03-02) 9-11am PT — let me know a time.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anna Bergstrom <anna.bergstrom@healthcareinc.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Healthcare Inc Procurement <procurement@healthcareinc.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today's discovery call

Hi all — thanks for the quick responses and public next steps. To keep momentum for a Q1 decision, proposed immediate action items:

1) Anna / procurement to confirm procurement lead and preferred PO / contract timing. Procurement, please advise if DocuSign BAA (link below) works: https://docuSign.com/envelope/BAA-HealthcareInc-12345
2) Marissa/Rishi to produce pricing estimates for: Dedicated (committed monthly GPU) and Private VPC (setup + recurring).
3) Dev to run a short technical review on Tue 2026-03-02 at 9:30am PT to review the PHI dataflow. Confirmed?
4) I'll attach a draft BAA for your legal to review (draft-baa.docx).

Items I'm attaching / linking for your review:
- SOC2 Type II attestation: https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/compliance/soc2-type2-2025.pdf
- Draft BAA: draft-baa.docx (attached)
- Sample SOW/POC template: dap-sow-template.docx (attached)

If PHI will be processed but not stored on our managed storage, Dedicated should be viable and is typically faster to spin up. If Healthcare Inc requires that no PHI ever be stored on Redwood-managed systems, we'll need Private VPC or on-prem and there will be an additional setup timeline (2-6 weeks depending on connectivity and procurement).

Can procurement confirm which option they prefer for initial pricing (Dedicated vs Private VPC) so I can get a formal quote out today?

Best,
